source.title: Visualizing the loss landscape of Self-supervised Vision Transformer
source.authors: Youngwan Lee; Jeffrey Willette; Jonghee Kim; Sung Ju Hwang

record.file_problem: Full text supplied, including appendix; no apparent truncation affecting the reported results.
record.tranche_reason: Qualitatively compares loss-landscape curvature with downstream performance, but does not measure training–test gaps or quantitatively test the version's specified sharpness measure.
record.gate_note: The paper reports qualitative loss-landscape comparisons and downstream task results. The landscapes are shown in figures and described in text; Table 1 reports downstream performance. No random-label or memorization experiment is reported.
record.test_reason: The study compares qualitative ViT loss landscapes and downstream performance. It does not test V7's relationship between magnitude-aware training-error perturbation tolerance and training–test gaps. Filter-normalized loss slices evaluated on ImageNetV2, sometimes under different objectives, measure a related construct. No other claim version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' qualitative conclusions: MAE has smoother, wider loss geometry than supervised ViT, and an EMA teacher widens MAE's convex regions. The authors attribute faster convergence to this geometry, but the convergence-speed evidence is cited from Lee et al. [25], rather than newly measured here. They explicitly defer quantitative analysis. Their additional claim that self-supervised models outperform supervised ViT on every downstream task conflicts with the supplied mask AP values.
record.recipe_differences: Studies self-supervised ViT pre-training and qualitative loss-landscape visualization rather than the claim versions' specified experiments; uses filter-wise normalization and compares different training objectives.
record.method_sensitivity: The compared training objective and weights change the landscapes: pre-training versus linear probing; MAE versus RC-MAE; masked reconstruction versus classification loss.

fits_no_version.finding: MAE has qualitatively smoother, wider loss contours than supervised ViT; RC-MAE has wider convex regions than MAE during pre-training and linear probing.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: These ViT checkpoints differ in qualitative filter-normalized loss geometry on ImageNetV2. These observations do not establish a relationship between magnitude-aware sharpness and training–test gaps.

fits_no_version.finding: MAE and RC-MAE exceed supervised ViT in fine-tuning accuracy and bounding-box AP. The supplied mask AP column instead favors supervised ViT; linear-probing assignments are ambiguous.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: MAE-family pre-training improves some reported downstream ViT-Base metrics relative to supervised training, with task-dependent results in the supplied table.

record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2023 Workshop: Self-Supervised Learning - Theory and Practice
record.problems: The paper explicitly says its loss-landscape analyses are qualitative and that more conclusive quantitative experiments are future work. It does not measure train–test gaps or report uncertainty for the landscape comparisons. The flattened Table 1 does not clearly assign a linear-probing value to RC-MAE.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance under random versus natural labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and compensating recipe changes.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance measured by training error, its association with training–test gaps among similarly fitted networks, and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict labels apply because none of V1–V8 is tested. The absent V7 measurements are untested components, not missing extracted results. Preserve the reported mask AP numbers while flagging the internal inconsistency; the supplied text does not justify repairing them.

versions.untested_parts: Width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks trained from scratch.
Batch-size effects on the generalization gap.

The paper qualitatively compares curvature with downstream performance, but does not measure training–test gaps, quantify magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, compare its ranking with norm- or margin-based measures, or test CIFAR-10/SVHN.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.
